## The question

PDBBind gives crystal structures with measured Kd. PRODIGY predicts affinity
from a structure and is the baseline to beat. The hypothesis was that a richer
set of interface descriptors — buried area, hydrogen bonds, shape
complementarity, Rosetta interface energies, PLIP interaction counts — would
predict Kd better, and that AlphaFold models could stand in for crystal
structures so the method would work on complexes with no solved structure.

That is two claims: that predicted structures are good enough, and that
interface descriptors beat PRODIGY. The first largely holds. The second does
not, at this sample size.

## The benchmark set

```{python}
#| echo: false
s = lr.params(SELECTION)
sel = lr.read_output(SELECTION, "selection.tsv")
Markdown(
    f"{s['n_complexes']} two-chain X-ray complexes, each chain over "
    f"{s['min_chain_length_aa']} residues, with an exact Kd "
    f"{lr.cite(SELECTION, P)}. Selection seed `{s['selection_seed']}`; no "
    f"pair exceeded the {s['homology_cutoff_identity']:.0%} identity / "
    f"{s['homology_cutoff_coverage']:.0%} coverage homology cutoff.\n\n"
    f"Kd spans **{lr.num(SELECTION, 'kd_m_min'):.0e} M to "
    f"{lr.num(SELECTION, 'kd_m_max'):.0e} M** — about "
    f"{abs(lr.num(SELECTION, 'log10_kd_max') - lr.num(SELECTION, 'log10_kd_min')):.0f} orders of magnitude, "
    f"from 1 fM to 790 µM (n = {len(sel)})."
)
```

::: {.caveat}
That 12-order span is assembled from different publications using different
assay types. A rank correlation across it is measuring agreement between
heterogeneous experiments as much as anything structural. Recurating the set
is an [open question](../decisions.qmd#pdbbind-recuration).
:::

## Predicted structures: good enough, with four exceptions

```{python}
#| echo: false
a = lr.params(AF3)
q = lr.params(QUALITY)
dockq = lr.read_output(QUALITY, "bench20_dockq.csv")
conf = lr.read_output(QUALITY, "af3_confidence.tsv")
orig = dockq[dockq.kind == "original"]
rel = dockq[dockq.kind == "relaxed"]
Markdown(
    f"{a['n_complexes']} complexes x {a['models_per_complex']} models = "
    f"{a['total_models']} predictions {lr.cite(AF3, P)}, ipTM "
    f"{a['iptm_min']} to {a['iptm_max']} over {len(conf)} models.\n\n"
    f"Mean DockQ against the crystal structures is "
    f"**{orig.DockQ.mean():.3f}** before relaxation and "
    f"**{rel.DockQ.mean():.3f}** after, over {len(orig)} and {len(rel)} "
    f"models {lr.cite(QUALITY, P)} — a mean change of "
    f"{rel.DockQ.mean() - orig.DockQ.mean():+.3f}. "
    f"{q['complexes_medium_or_high']} of {q['n_complexes']} complexes reach "
    f"medium or high CAPRI accuracy."
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
per_complex = (
    dockq.pivot_table(index="complex", columns="kind", values="DockQ",
                      aggfunc="mean")
    .join(conf.groupby("complex_id").iptm.mean().rename("mean_iptm"))
    .sort_values("original")
)
per_complex["change"] = per_complex["relaxed"] - per_complex["original"]
per_complex.round(3)
```

Four complexes are wrong, and they are wrong in two different ways.

```{python}
#| echo: false
wrong = lr.as_list(QUALITY, "incorrect_complexes")
rows = per_complex.loc[[c for c in wrong if c in per_complex.index]]
Markdown(
    "Three — 1zvh, 3qhy, 5szj — are *honestly* wrong: low ipTM, low DockQ. "
    "The model knew it was guessing.\n\n"
    f"**5bnq is the problem case.** Mean ipTM "
    f"{rows.loc['5bnq', 'mean_iptm']:.2f} but DockQ "
    f"{rows.loc['5bnq', 'original']:.2f}, with fnat 0 in all five models. "
    "Confirmed by an independent alignment-based contact check, so it is not "
    "a chain-mapping artefact: it is a confidently wrong prediction. "
    "Confidence cannot be used as a filter on its own."
)
```

```{python}
rows.round(3)
```

A further caveat on comparing predictions to crystal at all:

```{python}
#| echo: false
Markdown(

)
```

## Correlations against experimental Kd

```{python}
#| echo: false
c = lr.params(CORR)
n20 = lr.read_output(CORR, "bench20_correlations.csv")
n17 = lr.read_output(CORR, "bench20_excl_lowiptm_correlations.csv")
n16 = lr.read_output(CORR, "bench20_excl_incorrect_correlations.csv")
Markdown(
    f"Three subsets {lr.cite(CORR, P)}: all {len(sel)} complexes; "
    f"{int(n17.n.iloc[0])} excluding the low-ipTM cases; and "
    f"{int(n16.n.iloc[0])} also excluding the confidently wrong 5bnq. "
    f"{len(n20)} features tested against experimental log₁₀ Kd by Spearman "
    f"and Kendall, with **no multiple-testing correction**."
)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
merged = (
    n20[["parameter", "spearman_rho", "spearman_pvalue"]]
    .merge(n17[["parameter", "spearman_rho", "spearman_pvalue"]],
           on="parameter", suffixes=("_n20", "_n17"))
    .merge(n16[["parameter", "spearman_rho", "spearman_pvalue"]]
           .rename(columns={"spearman_rho": "spearman_rho_n16",
                            "spearman_pvalue": "spearman_pvalue_n16"}),
           on="parameter")
    .set_index("parameter")
    .reindex(n20.set_index("parameter").spearman_rho.abs()
             .sort_values(ascending=False).index)
)
merged.round(3)
```

```{python}
#| echo: false
hb20 = n20[n20.parameter == "HB"].iloc[0]
hb16 = n16[n16.parameter == "HB"].iloc[0]
dg20 = n20[n20.parameter == "dG_norm"].iloc[0]
dg16 = n16[n16.parameter == "dG_norm"].iloc[0]
sig20 = int((n20.spearman_pvalue < 0.05).sum())
sig16 = int((n16.spearman_pvalue < 0.05).sum())
Markdown(
    f"**Interface hydrogen-bond count is the only feature passing "
    f"|rho| ≥ {c['abs_rho_threshold']} in all three subsets**: "
    f"{lr.fmt_rho(hb20.spearman_rho, int(hb20.n), hb20.spearman_pvalue)} "
    f"rising to "
    f"{lr.fmt_rho(hb16.spearman_rho, int(hb16.n), hb16.spearman_pvalue)}. "
    f"The sign is negative, so more hydrogen bonds goes with lower log₁₀ Kd, "
    f"i.e. tighter binding — the direction one would hope for.\n\n"
    f"`dG_norm` is the runner-up and strengthens as wrong models are removed: "
    f"{lr.fmt_rho(dg20.spearman_rho, int(dg20.n), dg20.spearman_pvalue)} to "
    f"{lr.fmt_rho(dg16.spearman_rho, int(dg16.n), dg16.spearman_pvalue)}.\n\n"
    f"**Features reaching p < 0.05 by Spearman: {sig20} of {len(n20)} at "
    f"n = 20, {sig16} of {len(n16)} at n = 16.** None. Across "
    f"{len(n20)} features at these sample sizes, nothing here would survive "
    f"a correction for multiple comparisons, and the strengthening of "
    f"`dG_norm` as cases are dropped is equally consistent with real signal "
    f"recovered from structural error and with noise at n = 16."
)
```

### Against the baseline

```{python}
#| echo: false
pvr = lr.read_output(CORR, "bench20_prodigy_crystal_vs_relaxed.csv")
Markdown(
    f"| Predictor | Spearman rho vs experimental log₁₀ Kd | n |\n"
    f"|---|---|---|\n"
    f"| PRODIGY on crystal structures (baseline) | "
    f"{c['prodigy_crystal_rho_n20']:+.3f}, not significant | {len(pvr)} |\n"
    f"| PRODIGY on relaxed AF3 models | "
    f"{c['prodigy_relaxed_rho_n20']:+.3f}, not significant | {len(pvr)} |\n"
    f"| Best interface feature (H-bond count) | "
    f"{hb20.spearman_rho:+.3f}, p = {hb20.spearman_pvalue:.2f}, "
    f"not significant | {int(hb20.n)} |\n\n"
    f"PRODIGY's own predictions agree between crystal and relaxed models at "
    f"rho = {c['prodigy_crystal_vs_relaxed_rho']} (n = {len(pvr)}) "
    f"{lr.cite(CORR, P)}, so swapping crystal structures for relaxed "
    f"predictions does not much change what PRODIGY says — which supports "
    f"the predicted-structures-are-usable claim while saying nothing good "
    f"about accuracy against experiment."
)
```

## Where this leaves the track

The interface-descriptor hypothesis is **not supported** by this benchmark.
The honest summary is that at n = 16–20, with a Kd range spanning 12 orders of
magnitude and mixed assay provenance, this experiment cannot distinguish a
weak real signal from noise. H-bond count is the only candidate worth
carrying forward.

Modelling (LASSO / Ridge / ElasticNet) and held-out validation are **not
started**, and should not start on these features at this sample size —
fitting a regularised model to 11 features and 16–20 points, selected after
inspecting correlations, would produce a number with no evidential value.

What would change the answer: a larger and better-curated benchmark with
consistent assay provenance and a narrower Kd range. That is the
[PDBBind recuration question](../decisions.qmd#pdbbind-recuration). Separately,
the [AlphaFold Server terms](../decisions.qmd#alphafold-terms) block
publication of anything here regardless of the result.
